- Remove the y ticks and y tick labels of the box-plot panel entirely.
- Label the x axis of the histogram.
- Make the figure 9 by 7 inches.
- The histogram's y axis must start at 0.
Save the figure as figure.png.

{"command": "cat <<'EOF' > plot.py
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv", encoding="utf-8-sig")
values = df.iloc[:, 1].dropna().to_numpy()
q1, med, q3 = np.percentile(values, [25, 50, 75])

fig, (ax_box, ax_hist) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 7), sharex=True, gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [1, 3], "hspace": 0.05})
ax_box.boxplot(values, vert=False, widths=0.6, patch_artist=True, boxprops={"facecolor": "lightsteelblue"}, medianprops={"color": "red"})
ax_box.set_yticks([])
ax_box.set_ylim(0.4, 1.6)
for spine in ax_box.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)
ax_box.tick_params(axis="x", bottom=False, labelbottom=False)
for k, (value, name, align) in enumerate([(q1, "Q1", "right"), (med, "Median", "center"), (q3, "Q3", "left")]):
    ax_box.text(value, 1.42, f" {name} = {value:.0f} ", ha=align, va="bottom", fontsize=9, color="darkred")
ax_box.text(values.min(), 0.55, f"Min = {values.min():.0f}", ha="left", va="top", fontsize=9)
ax_box.text(values.max(), 0.55, f"Max = {values.max():.0f}", ha="right", va="top", fontsize=9)

ax_hist.hist(values, bins=25, color="lightsteelblue", edgecolor="white")
ax_hist.set_ylim(0, None)
for value in (q1, med, q3):
    ax_box.axvline(value, color="red", linestyle="-", linewidth=1.2, clip_on=False, ymin=-0.1, ymax=0.75)
    ax_hist.axvline(value, color="red", linestyle="-", linewidth=1.2, clip_on=False, ymin=0, ymax=1.03)
ax_hist.set_xlabel("Women's earnings (millions of dollars)")
ax_hist.set_ylabel("Frequency")
ax_box.set_title("Distribution of women's earnings")
fig.savefig("figure.png")
EOF
"}
